description:

No real daemon, IDE, launcher, watcher, scheduled start, process, handle or access path was stopped, denied, signalled or killed. The only 'kill' matches are comments saying it does not kill anything."

The harness is real, useful work and is not in question. What is missing is the run it was built to perform.

THE DANGER THIS TASK CLOSES. task-09008b4c (GA activation record) requires "a SUCCESSFUL Legacy quiesce drill" plus its own GO_ACTIVATE. A readiness sweep that resolves that clause by task id reads task-4e1fe696 = DONE and concludes the drill ran. I ran exactly that scan on 2026-08-15 and it reported task-09008b4c as having NO unmet dependencies. It has two. An id-resolution scan structurally cannot see a prose human-authority gate, and the emptier the id match, the greener the false result. Without this task on the board there is nothing a scan CAN see that says the quiesce has not happened.

WHY IT IS BLOCKED RATHER THAN CLAIMABLE — four gates, three measured unmet today:
1. explicit human GO_QUIESCE — NOT GIVEN. I searched every channel in .moe/messages: five messages mention GO_QUIESCE, all sender=system, zero human-authored. QA searched independently and found the same.
2. task-22cfca91 Portability shadow gate — PLANNING, not DONE, and in a different epic.
3. task-0c89476b Disaster restore proof — BLOCKED.
4. Deterministic legacy importer — resolve by title before planning; not separately measured here.

SCOPE WHEN UNBLOCKED: perform the quiesce against the real system using the landed harness, and record what was actually stopped — process, handle, watcher, scheduled start and access path — as evidence, not as assertion. NOT IN SCOPE: rebuilding or re-scoping the harness (task-4e1fe696 owns it and it is DONE), the GA activation record itself, or granting any authority this task is waiting on.

Verification: to be defined at planning time against the real hosts, and it must not be a sandbox run. A green pnpm test:migration is NOT evidence the legacy system was quiesced.
definitionOfDone: The quiesce is performed against the REAL system, not a fixture tree: the evidence names each actual process, handle, watcher, scheduled start and access path that was stopped or denied, with the observation that proved each one stopped.

A human has given GO_QUIESCE in writing, recorded on this board with the principal and the moment, before any stop action is taken - never inferred from a task status, an instruction to avoid blocking, or a scope-narrowing decision.
Any path that cannot be quiesced is reported as an explicit refusal with its exact stable reason code and the layer that refused, never omitted from the evidence and never reported as success.
The evidence distinguishes a live run from a harness run on its face, so no future reader or automated sweep can mistake one for the other - this task exists because that distinction was lost once.
task-09008b4c (GA activation record) can cite THIS task's live evidence rather than task-4e1fe696's harness status as its quiesce dependency.
taskRails: Do not run any stop action before a human GO_QUIESCE is recorded on this board. An instruction to avoid blocking, to plan production-way, or to keep the fleet busy is NOT a GO_QUIESCE - that exact conflation is why this task exists.
A green pnpm test:migration proves the harness works. It is not evidence the legacy system was quiesced, and it may not be presented as such in any completion report.
Do not rebuild, re-scope or re-approve the harness. task-4e1fe696 owns it, it is DONE, and it was approved at harness scope deliberately. Compose it; do not duplicate it.
Report what was actually stopped, observed one by one. An assertion that a class of thing was stopped, without a per-item observation, is the proof-of-shapes failure Clause 2 forbids.
Re-measure all four gates before planning - GO_QUIESCE, task-22cfca91, task-0c89476b and the deterministic legacy importer. This reason is a snapshot and this board moves fast.

implementationPlan.description:
STEP 3 — THE ACTOR MODULE, TDD. NEW tests/migration/cutover-live/live-quiesce-actor.test.ts first, then live-quiesce-actor.ts (<=250 lines). This module is BUILT here and RUN by nothing until step 8; it takes no action at import time.

`quiesceItem(item, ports)` performs the stop appropriate to the item's kind through INJECTED ports — the tests inject fakes, and step 5's entry supplies the real implementations — returning either `{ ok: true, item, observedAfter, observation }` or a refusal `{ code, layer, item }`.

THE CONTRACT, straight from rails 3-4 and DoD 1/3, and it is the whole point of the module: THE RESULT IS DERIVED FROM AN OBSERVATION TAKEN AFTER THE STOP — re-query the process, handle, watcher, scheduled start or path and record what came back — NEVER from the stop command's own exit code. A stop command that exits 0 while the thing is still running is the ordinary case on Windows, not an exotic one.
- an item whose post-observation still shows it live returns `LIVE_QUIESCE_ITEM_STILL_LIVE`;
- an item that cannot be stopped at all returns `LIVE_QUIESCE_ITEM_UNDENIABLE` with the layer that refused;
- neither may be omitted, and neither may be upgraded to success (DoD 3).

`quiesceAll` returns ONE result per input item and asserts the output length equals the input length. A class-level summary such as "all processes stopped" must be UNREPRESENTABLE because no such return shape exists — that is rail 4 enforced by the type, not by discipline.

DIVERGENCE ARM (epic rail): a fake port whose stop command EXITS 0 while the post-observation still reports the item live must yield `LIVE_QUIESCE_ITEM_STILL_LIVE`. State in the file header which other mechanisms this fixture crosses and why none of them can answer first — the item is well-formed, the roster admits its kind, and `discoveredBy` is present, so the post-observation check is the only thing that can refuse. An implementation that trusts the exit code passes every other arm and reds exactly here.

THE CONTRACT IS ENFORCED STRUCTURALLY. `StopAttempt.exitCode` is recorded for the transcript and is read by NO branch in the module — I checked by reading the file back; the only consumer of `attempt` after the accepted-check is `attempt.command`. `accepted: true` means the command was issued and not refused outright, which is a deliberately different claim from "the thing stopped". Only the post-stop observation decides.

DESIGN CHANGE FORCED BY A MEASUREMENT, disclosed because it is not in the plan's text. serena mem:gotcha-taskkill-returns-before-the-os-reaps-the-pid records that on THIS host `taskkill /PID n /T /F` returns roughly 78ms BEFORE the pid leaves `tasklist` — 8/8 samples, min 68ms, max 100ms, every pid eventually gone. The kill is asynchronous: taskkill exits once the kill is REQUESTED. A single post-stop sample would therefore refuse nearly every REAL process stop with a false LIVE_QUIESCE_ITEM_STILL_LIVE, which would make the live run's evidence worthless in the permissive-looking direction (a run full of spurious refusals invites someone to relax the check). So the observation POLLS to `OBSERVATION_POLL_BUDGET = 200`. The budget counts POLLS, not milliseconds, so the bound is deterministic across hosts and suite load; a genuinely stopped item leaves on poll 1-2, so the budget is only ever spent on the failing path. Arm "tolerates the measured Windows reap delay" pins this: a port live for 3 polls then dead returns ok with `pollsUsed === 4`.
This does NOT weaken the divergence property. A port that never reports the item gone exhausts all 200 polls and still refuses.

DIVERGENCE ARM (epic rail) — and the file header states what it crosses, as required. In "a stop that exits 0 while the item stays live": the item is well-formed, its kind is on the roster, `discoveredBy` and `observedBefore` are present, and the stop port neither throws nor refuses. So none of the inventory's six refusals can fire; LIVE_QUIESCE_ITEM_UNDENIABLE cannot fire because the stop was accepted; LIVE_QUIESCE_OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE cannot fire because the probe answers cleanly. The post-stop observation is the ONLY mechanism left that can refuse. An implementation returning ok on `exitCode === 0` passes all eight other arms and reds exactly there. Drilled as D1 in step 7.

THREE REFUSALS, each with an arm asserting the exact code AND the layer: LIVE_QUIESCE_ITEM_STILL_LIVE (budget exhausted; detail names the budget so an exhausted run is distinguishable from one unlucky sample), LIVE_QUIESCE_ITEM_UNDENIABLE (carries `refusedByLayer` from the port — the arm asserts "windows-scm", not merely that something refused, since this layer and the host layer can both refuse), LIVE_QUIESCE_OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE (probe threw; an unobservable item is never reported as stopped). Roster frozen at exactly 3 with set-equality both directions.

THE SWEEP CANNOT SUMMARIZE A CLASS. `quiesceAll` returns one `QuiesceItemResult` per input with `inputCount` and `resultCount` recorded side by side, so a dropped item is visible rather than inferred. There is no return shape capable of carrying "all processes stopped" — rail 4 enforced by the type. Sweep arm states its denominator explicitly (5 = LIVE_QUIESCE_KINDS.length, asserted twice) so a sweep generating zero cases cannot pass vacuously.

ONE ADDITION BEYOND THE PLAN, disclosed: `SweepOutcome` has a third member `EMPTY`. An empty input is not COMPLETE — nothing was stopped, so nothing is proven — and COMPLETE/PARTIAL alone would have made a zero-item sweep report success. `PARTIAL` is what step 5's point 7 needs: the arm proves a refused item SURVIVES into the sweep rather than being dropped, which is the DoD-3 outcome.

A PARTIAL RUN IS ACCEPTED, NOT REFUSED. Its arm proves the refusal SURVIVES into the record carrying its own code and layer — asserts `code === "LIVE_QUIESCE_ITEM_STILL_LIVE"` and `layer === "live-quiesce-actor"`, i.e. the actor's layer, not this one, so a reader can tell which layer refused. An honest partial with named refusals is the DoD 3 outcome; omitting the item is the failure this row exists to prevent.
